content:
- Model consistently underestimates true values, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a strong upward trend (increasing) while true values exhibit sharp downward spikes and volatility, suggesting model fails to capture sudden drops.
- Model overreacts to recent high values (e.g., after a spike), forecasting higher prices than true outcome.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecasts gradually increase toward a “neutral” level, but true values often deviate sharply downward after initial peaks.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–2 days in the early part of the window, then catch up or overshoot.
- Model fails to account for sharp, non-linear corrections after spikes — true values often drop sharply after a forecasted peak.
- Forecasts are overly smooth and lack volatility matching observed true values, especially in the middle to late part of the 30-day window.
- Model tends to overestimate the “average” or “trend” of the 30-day window, ignoring short-term volatility and sharp corrections.
